---
title: "What Gamma(1, 1) actually says"
subtitle: "Catalog M-07"
description: "Five readings of the default Gamma(1, 1) hyperprior: vague about alpha, but not vague about clusters."
toc: false
---

Gamma(1, 1) is the usual "vague" default for the concentration parameter. It is vague
about alpha: the prior spreads alpha over two orders of magnitude. It is not vague about
clusters. Read through the Chinese restaurant process and stick-breaking, the same prior
makes definite statements about how many clusters there are, how large the cluster of a
random unit is, and how likely it is that everyone shares one cluster.

## Five readings at J = 100

1. **alpha.** Pr(alpha ≤ .5) = .393: two in five draws of alpha are small enough that a new
   table is rarely opened.
2. **Number of clusters.** E K_100 = 4.84 with a 90% interval of [1, 12]. Change J and this
   tile moves: 2.65 at J = 10, 6.44 at J = 500, 8.73 at J = 5000 (for J above 500 the band
   is precomputed in R).
3. **Size of a random unit's cluster.** Pr(W_SB > .5) = .591 and Pr(W_SB > .9) = .303, at
   every J.
4. **Seventy-nine sites, twenty times.** Simulated sets of 79 sites (the STAR schools) show
   the typical pattern: one large cluster and a few small ones, and now and then a single
   cluster for all 79.
5. **Prior collapse.** P(K_100 = 1) = .168: before any data, the prior gives about one chance
   in six that all 100 units form a single cluster.

The literature presets move all five tiles at once. Gamma(1, 3) puts more mass near
alpha = 0: Pr(W_SB > .5) = .812. Gamma(0.037, 0.037), the SCAL shortcut of
[Part 3](../problems/method-problems-strip.qmd), is vaguer still about alpha and gives
P(K_100 = 1) = .834.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Vague in alpha is not vague in clusters.** A flat-looking prior on the concentration
parameter is a strong prior on the partition. The value .834 for Gamma(0.037, 0.037) at
J = 100 comes from an adaptive integral in R and from this page's engine; an earlier .824
came from a coarse 80-node quadrature and is not used. These are prior statements. K_J is
the number of fitted components (occupied clusters) among the J units.
:::
